name: Grandma Reviews Gadgets
blurb: Grandma reviews a smart speaker with brutal logic, until it fails her one real question
title: Grandma Reviews Gadgets: 60-Second Comedy Script for 2
description: A 60-second vertical comedy script for 2: a grandma reviews a smart speaker with brutal, loving logic until it fails her one real question. Free to film.
h1: Grandma Reviews Gadgets: a 60-Second Comedy Script for 2 People
logline: A grandchild films Grandma's first ever tech review: a smart speaker with no buttons and, in her opinion, no manners. She tests it with her own logic and it loses every round. Then she asks it the one question that actually matters to her.
setting: A living room sofa in daylight. Props: a small smart speaker or any round object playing one, a phone to film.

roles.name: Grandma
roles.note: 60s to 80s, dignified, deadpan, secretly delighted to be filmed; works just as well as Grandpa.

roles.name: Sam
roles.note: Teen to 20s, any gender, the grandchild behind the camera who wants the video to go well.

script.text: ON SCREEN: Grandma reviews gadgets. Episode 1.

script.action: GRANDMA sits upright on the sofa. A small smart speaker waits on the table like a guest she does not trust.

script.say: Okay, Grandma, we're recording. Review it.
This is a speaker. It has no buttons. Already suspicious.
I talk to the kettle. The kettle doesn't answer. That's why we get along.

script.action: She leans in close and shouts.

script.sfx: A chime. A flat robot voice: Sunny, twenty-four degrees.

script.say: I have a window. Two stars.
So does the neighbour. Through the wall. For free.
Fine. Speaker. When is Sam visiting again?

script.sfx: A chime. The robot voice: You have no upcoming events.

script.action: Grandma stares at the speaker. Then straight into the lens.

script.say: Don't put it in. Just come.

script.action: She pats the speaker like a small dog.

script.say: The speaker gets two stars. My grandchild gets five.

body: Shoot vertical 9:16 with the phone held by the person playing Sam, at sitting eye level, so Grandma's looks into the lens feel like she is talking to the viewer. Sit her facing a window for soft, flattering light and turn off the TV and fans so the dialogue is clean. Play the speaker's voice from a second phone in the room, or add it in the edit with a caption. Do three or four takes and keep the one where the soft question sounds least performed.

ul: Grandma never tries to be funny. She is completely sure her logic is correct, and that certainty is the joke.
Give each star rating a short pause before it, as if she is judging a cooking contest.
The turn is the question about Sam. Drop the volume, look at the speaker, not the camera, and let it be a real question.
After the speaker fails, hold the silence for a full second before looking into the lens. Do not rush to the next line.
Sam should sound like a real grandchild: a little embarrassed, a little proud. Keep the voice warm, not mocking.
Common mistake: playing Grandma as confused by technology. She understands it fine. She just does not respect it.
Swap the gadget for wireless earbuds, a fitness watch or a robot vacuum, and keep the same three tests: what it does, what she already has, and the one thing it cannot do.
Cast a grandpa, or two grandparents on the sofa who disagree on every rating before agreeing on the last one.
Make it a series: each episode a new gadget, and each ending another small way of asking the grandchild to visit.

faq.q: Can I post this on a monetised channel?
faq.a: Yes. The script is free to film and perform under CC BY 4.0, including on monetised channels. Just credit "Script: cv.cm" in the caption or description.

faq.q: My grandparent does not speak English. Can they still do it?
faq.a: Yes, and it often works better. Let them say each line in their own language and their own words, keep the speaker lines and the star ratings, and add subtitles.

faq.q: What if I do not own a smart speaker?
faq.a: Use any small round object as the speaker and play the robot voice from a second phone, or add it as a caption in the edit. Viewers accept the prop as long as Grandma takes it seriously.
